author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: The Open API is pull only, the controller's syslog has no published format, and its webhook can't add the Authorization header, so these parsers read the records the example bridge in bridges/tp-link-omada-logs reads from the Omada Open API and posts to HTTP Ingest, with omada_record (event, alert or audit) first, then omada_scope, omada_id and the customer and site. Give the bridge an Open API application in client mode with a role that can only view; in MSP mode it reads the MSP view, each customer and each customer's sites. Events and alerts are routed by their log key, from TP-Link's log notification key table: controller and hotspot operator sign-ins, portal and 802.1X authentication and remote PPTP and L2TP clients go to Auth (an _OK key as a logon, _FL as a failure, OSG_RC_VPN_LO as a logoff); gateway attack detections and rogue DHCP servers go to Thirdparty, with the key's name as the title, the content as the summary and an alert's level as the severity (Error high, Warning medium, Information low; an event, which has no level, is medium). Every audit log goes to Management Event with the operator, address, audit type, content, label and result. Other events and alerts stay generic. The time is the record's time in milliseconds. How sure this is: the record fields, the key names and the audit types come from TP-Link's Omada Open API reference and Open API Access Guide. TP-Link doesn't catalog the content text, so the user, client and address in it aren't read: the content goes to event_metadata (and to the failure reason of a failure), and the samples' content text is made up. The site name is the target host. Samples are made up in the shape the bridge sends. The parsers passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-16: each child combined with the parent into one parser (127 of 127 fields matched the emulator in each of 3 runs), and each child as a separate parser under its parent (121 of 121 fields, each record taken in 5 of 5 runs, and the parent-only records matched). No built-in parser claimed these records in 3 runs.
